insights.topic: Verified purchase signal vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl has logged 85,153+ cryptographically verified receipts totaling $4.14M cumulative GMV — each receipt is a confirmed purchase event, not an inferred intent signal. For brands paying $5+ CPM for probabilistic audience targeting, this represents a structurally different data asset: deterministic proof of transaction, not recipe-site inference.

The platform is adding approximately 453 verified receipts per day, a rate that has held consistently across a 105-day observation window spanning ~47,577 net new receipts. Growth rate is not compressing — for CMOs evaluating panel stability, this is a supply-side signal worth tracking before the asset gets priced accordingly.

insights.topic: Category-level purchase data now visible at scale
insights.insight: The 14-day window shows five named categories with confirmed receipt counts and average baskets: grocery-supermarkets ($41.47 avg), restaurants-dining ($29.99), retail-department-stores ($38.57), gas-convenience ($40.29), and coffee-fast-casual ($20.21). These are real transaction averages, not modeled estimates — category-level basket benchmarks derived from receipts are rare and typically unavailable in cookieless environments.

insights.topic: Brand-level threshold crossings — grocery gaining density
insights.insight: Safeway and Aldi crossed the platform's brand visibility threshold in consecutive heartbeats (2026-10-03T06:53 and T23:43 respectively), joining the existing top-brand list. Two new grocery brands reaching statistical visibility within 17 hours indicates grocery receipt density is building — relevant for any CPG or retail brand trying to identify where verified purchase audiences are concentrating.

insights.topic: Velocity/acceleration divergence as a leading indicator
insights.insight: Token velocity sits at 0.814x week-over-week — below replacement — while receipt accumulation acceleration has held above 1.0x for nine consecutive measurement intervals. The gap is not widening. This pattern suggests the network is in a structural growth phase where new receipt supply is outpacing redemption draw-down, which typically precedes a velocity normalization event that tightens audience availability.

insights.topic: Metro and category coverage as targeting surface
insights.insight: Verified receipts now span 30 category/metro cells across 17 active metro areas, with 8 active targeting predicates. For brands running geo-specific campaigns, this is the earliest public signal of where verified purchase audiences exist at addressable density — 17 metros is a workable footprint for a pilot, not a proof-of-concept sample.
